statistical_method: 10类别聚合比例；无显著性检验

statistical_method: 每层二元成功比例；分母未在Table 3注释逐层列出

comparison: GPT-o1 vs CAP powered by GPT-o1
statistical_method: ROC-AUC against human labels；8 uniformly sampled frames；无区间或检验

comparison: SA/PC ROC-AUC across two component ablations

comparison: Event vs Physics-enhanced vs Detailed within model
statistical_method: 成功比例；未报告paired confidence interval或test

statistical_method: human-evaluated pass/total；未说明配对检验

claim: 复杂多对象/多力提示比简化配对更难。
statistical_method: human-evaluated pass/total；未说明配对检验

claim: 高质量模型更常以静态场景回避困难运动。
statistical_method: failure-case conditional rate；每模型固定50个失败样本，无抽样区间

claim: 同架构更大模型总体上略优，但并非每个层级指标单调。
value: Cosmos overall Both 0.184 vs 0.178; CogVideo 0.163 vs 0.150
statistical_method: 点估计对照；无重复运行或不确定性

claim: CAP fine-tuning在80/20 split上进一步提高Qwen与GPT-4o。
statistical_method: 单一80/20 split点估计；split unit与seed未报告

claim: CAP与human leaderboard大体一致，但Sora/Kling第二名次序互换。
value: Human: Sora second; CAP: Kling second
statistical_method: rank comparison，无rank uncertainty

claim: Standardized datasets show wide trajectory and action heterogeneity.
value: Average rounds 10.1; range 1.0–26.8; overall A/C/M 53/24/23; thought coverage 83.8%.
statistical_method: Dataset-level descriptive point summaries; no dispersion or inferential test.
adverse_explanation: Descriptive differences do not establish data quality or downstream utility.

claim: ADP improves SWE-Bench Verified for SWE-Agent across three model sizes.
comparison: Matched harness and base model at 7B/14B/32B
statistical_method: Accuracy point estimates and absolute percentage-point subtraction; no uncertainty.
adverse_explanation: Seed variation and benchmark denominators are not reported.

claim: ADP improves SWE-Bench Verified for OpenHands across three model sizes.
comparison: Matched harness and base model at 7B/14B/32B
statistical_method: Accuracy point estimates; no uncertainty.
adverse_explanation: Domain-filtered non-web training narrows the cross-domain interpretation.

claim: ADP improves WebArena for AgentLab across three model sizes.
comparison: Matched harness and base model at 7B/14B/32B
statistical_method: Accuracy point estimates; no uncertainty.
adverse_explanation: AgentLab is trained only on the web portion, not the whole cross-domain corpus.

claim: ADP exceeds each listed base on AgentBench OS, but ADP accuracy is not monotonic from 7B to 14B.
statistical_method: Accuracy point estimates; no uncertainty.
adverse_explanation: The phrase monotonic gains applies to selected delta curves, not trained accuracy on every benchmark.

claim: ADP gives a small reported gain on GAIA at 7B.
statistical_method: Single accuracy point estimate; no larger models or uncertainty.

claim: The paper reports an average improvement of about 20% over corresponding base models.
statistical_method: Aggregation formula, included comparisons, weights, and uncertainty are not reported.
adverse_explanation: Large and small point differences are compressed into one undefined average.

claim: ADP mixtures outperform task-specific mixtures in five matched configurations.
value: SWE 10.4 vs 1.0; SWE Qwen-3 16.6 vs 11.0/0.2; WebArena 20.1 vs 16.0; AgentBench 25.7 vs 21.5; GAIA 9.1 vs 0.6.
comparison: Same harness+model, ADP versus task-specific data
statistical_method: Accuracy point estimates; no uncertainty or multi-comparison procedure.
adverse_explanation: The prose mentions Base, but Table 6 contains no Base rows, so negative transfer below base is not identified.

claim: ADP retains an advantage at approximately matched sample count.
comparison: Qwen-3-8B ADP versus upsampled SWE-smith on SWE-Bench/OpenHands
statistical_method: One matched-scale accuracy comparison; no uncertainty.
adverse_explanation: Diversity, source content, conversion, and sampling weights remain bundled.

claim: The hub-and-spoke pipeline lowers modeled converter LOC at A=100.
value: 489,200 LOC without ADP versus 12,592 with ADP; measured inputs are 4,892 Raw→ADP LOC and ≈77 mean ADP→SFT LOC.
comparison: Modeled no-ADP versus ADP community cost
statistical_method: Deterministic LOC accounting with proxy and hypothetical A=100 extrapolation.
adverse_explanation: Only three harness converters are observed, and Raw→ADP LOC proxies Raw→SFT LOC.

claim: Large LeanPremise improves Mathlib retrieval and end-to-end proof rate over older selectors.
comparison: MePo: 42.1% / 26.3% / 27.5%; ReProver: 38.7% / 12.0% / 22.3% for the same columns
statistical_method: Theorem-level average ground-truth recall and proof-rate percentages; no inferential test or uncertainty interval.

claim: Ground-truth premises define an empirical best-case ceiling for the pipeline.
value: Ground truth proof rates: aesop 27.7%, auto 33.1%, aesop+auto 37.8%, full 41.0%, cumul 43.0%
statistical_method: Conditional theorem-level proof-rate comparison; no uncertainty interval.

claim: Model scaling and accumulation produce complementary gains.
value: recall@32 small→medium→large 67.8→68.1→72.7%; full 27.9→28.5→30.1%; cumulative full 34.5%, cumul 37.3%; cumulative∪MePo full 38.2%, cumul 39.6%
comparison: Each value is compared within Table 2 settings; union/cumulative sets outperform single large model in proof rate
statistical_method: Direct table-percentage comparisons; no between-model significance test.

claim: Pipeline variants trade cost and ability, and cumul can recover cases missed by full.
value: Mean runtime auto 4.3s, aesop 0.92s, aesop+auto 4.9s, full 6.6s; cumul can exceed full
comparison: Variant proof rates are compared in Table 2; cumul tries all four variants
statistical_method: Mean theorem runtime and proof-rate percentages; no runtime dispersion.

claim: LeanHammer transfers to miniCTX-v2-test on average beyond the no-premise baseline.
value: Full average: None 14.9%, LeanPremise large 20.7%, Ground truth 26.1%; large split values 0.0/16.0/36.4/38.0/10.0/24.0%
comparison: Six splits: Carleson, ConNF, FLT, Foundation, HepLean, Seymour
statistical_method: Split-level theorem proof rates and reported average; no uncertainty or inferential test.

claim: The paper's robust-generalization claim is based on large/full performance relative to ground truth.
value: Mathlib 73.5% and miniCTX 79.4% of corresponding ground-truth full proof rates
comparison: Relative ratios are derived from Table 2 and Table 3; Carleson remains 0.0% and Foundation equals None at 38.0%
statistical_method: Derived ratio of proof-rate percentages; no uncertainty interval.

claim: LeanPremise improves over MePo on the authors' relative comparison.
value: Large recall@32 is 73% higher relative to MePo; large cumul proof rate is about 21% higher
comparison: Table 2: 72.7% vs 42.1% recall@32 and 33.3% vs 27.5% cumul
statistical_method: Relative differences of table percentages; no inferential test.

claim: LeanHammer using the large model outperforms retrained ReProver in proof rate.
value: About 150% more theorems in full and 50% more in cumul; large is 82M parameters versus ReProver 218M
statistical_method: Theorem percentages on authors' train/valid/test splits and updated Mathlib; no inferential test.

claim: Removing hammer-aware extraction, negative sampling, or positive masking generally degrades Mathlib-valid performance.
comparison: Table 4 compares each ablation with medium baseline and Ground truth; −loss-mask cumul is the one higher single column
statistical_method: Mathlib-valid ablation percentages; no repeated-run uncertainty; author labels the anomalous cumul as noise.

claim: Every tested model degrades on every main task under SHARDED, with 39% average degradation.
value: P is described as approximately 90 in FULL and 65 in SHARDED; Table 1 aggregates a -39% degradation.
comparison: SHARDED versus FULL across 15 models and six tasks.
statistical_method: Per-instruction mean over 10 simulations, then corpus/task/model aggregation; no inferential interval or formal test reported.
author_interpretation: The matched multi-turn setting exposes capability hidden by fully specified evaluation.

claim: CONCAT largely preserves FULL performance, supporting information preservation under rephrased shards.
statistical_method: Aggregate performance ratio across main tasks/models; no uncertainty interval.
author_interpretation: SHARDED loss is not explained by information loss in the shard wording.

claim: Stronger models get lost at a similar relative rate to weaker models.
value: Average degradations for named strong models are 30-40%.
comparison: Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5, GPT-4.1 versus smaller models.
statistical_method: Relative degradation aggregated across six tasks; denominator depends on each model's FULL score.
author_interpretation: Single-turn strength does not prevent multi-turn degradation.

claim: The average degradation is dominated by unreliability rather than aptitude loss.
value: Aptitude drops 16%; unreliability increases 112%; fixed-instruction best-to-worst runs differ by 50 points on average.
statistical_method: Per-instruction 90th percentile and 90th-minus-10th percentile range, averaged across corpora.
author_interpretation: Lost in Conversation is principally a reliability phenomenon.

claim: The main effect appears once instructions span two or more turns in the gradual experiment.
value: Both GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini show a large reliability increase from two shards onward.
statistical_method: 10 simulations per instruction/model; 31 claimed source instructions expanded to 248 variants, though Appendix L contains a conflicting 'eight instructions' sentence.
author_interpretation: Providing everything at once is the only tested granularity that restores reliability.

claim: Later first answer attempts are associated with higher performance on Code and Math.
value: 30.9 for first attempt in the first 20% versus 64.4 in the last 20%.
comparison: Earliest versus latest first-answer timing bins.
statistical_method: Conversations binned by normalized first-answer turn; averages across 15 models on two tasks.
author_interpretation: Premature answer attempts can plant incorrect assumptions.

claim: Answer attempts grow longer over turns and remain longer even when correct.
value: Final SHARDED attempts are 20-300% longer; correct Code is 27% longer and correct Database is 14% longer than FULL.
comparison: Successive SHARDED attempts versus FULL/CONCAT and correct-only subsets.
statistical_method: Mean extracted-answer character length by attempt index; filtered correct subset for Code/Database.
author_interpretation: Models retain invalid assumptions and bloat later solutions.

claim: Summary citations overweight first and last turns relative to middle turns.
value: At turn 8, 20% cite turn-8 documents versus 8% for turns 2 and 3.
comparison: Document introduction turn within eight-turn summaries.
statistical_method: Citation shares averaged across 15 models; row totals may be under 100% due to hallucinated citations.
author_interpretation: Loss-in-the-middle also occurs across conversation turns.

claim: More verbose conversations perform worse on five of six tasks.
value: Average P is 40.7 in the shortest quintile and 35.6 in the longest; task-level gains for short responses are described as 10-50%.
statistical_method: Ten runs split into five bins of two for each model-instruction pair, then averaged by task.
author_interpretation: Short responses avoid unnecessary assumptions and keep the conversation focused.

claim: RECAP and SNOWBALL help but do not restore FULL/CONCAT performance.
value: SNOWBALL mitigates 15-20% of the FULL-to-SHARDED deterioration; RECAP performs better but is operationally unrealistic.
statistical_method: 10 simulations on all instructions from four tasks for GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini.

claim: A system prompt warning produces only a small average change.
value: +1% average, with +1 to +3 on two tasks, +7 on one, and -6 on one.
comparison: GPT-4o SHARDED with versus without a multi-turn/underspecification hint.
statistical_method: Four-task performance comparison; no uncertainty interval.
author_interpretation: The hint changes behavior but does not prevent getting lost.

claim: Lowering temperature improves single-turn reliability much more than multi-turn reliability.
value: FULL/CONCAT U falls 50-80%; SHARDED remains around U=30 even with both temperatures at 0.
statistical_method: 20 runs per condition, 40 instructions, two models, four tasks.
author_interpretation: Small early nondeterminism cascades over turns.

claim: Document translation does not show the main degradation pattern.
value: FULL, CONCAT, and SHARDED BLEU remain within 10% for GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o.
comparison: Three simulation settings on 30 WMT 2019 document pairs.
statistical_method: BLEU on ten-sentence documents sharded two sentences per turn.
author_interpretation: The task is episodic and therefore not genuinely underspecified across turns.

claim: The simulator is usually valid under manual inspection.
value: Overall Success 97.8%; shard fully revealed 96.0%; strategy accuracy 95.2%; extraction success 97.0%.
comparison: Four inspected tasks and five validation criteria.
statistical_method: Manual annotation of a reported 200 conversations in prose versus 100 in Table 2 caption; no inter-annotator agreement statistic.
author_interpretation: Simulator error cannot explain degradation beyond roughly 2%.

claim: UHAT 与 B-RASP non-emptiness 均为 EXPSPACE-complete。
comparison: LTL satisfiability 的 PSPACE procedure 作为上界后端；2^N-tiling 作为 hardness source。
statistical_method: not_applicable；polynomial-time reduction + exponential UHAT/B-RASP→LTL translation + PSPACE LTL decision procedure。
author_interpretation: succinct descriptions make basic verification intractable.
adverse_explanation: 该 lower bound 依赖能编码巨大 counters 的 worst-case UHAT。

claim: 受限 strict-future/rightmost（或对偶）UHAT 仍有 EXPSPACE-hardness。
statistical_method: not_applicable；construction-preserving reduction。

claim: 任意 UHAT computation 的 value precision 对 |T| 仅需 polynomial bits。
statistical_method: not_applicable；denominator/numerator bit-length induction。

claim: UHAT 可在 exponential time 翻译为等价 LTL formula。
statistical_method: not_applicable；finite value enumeration and layer-wise formula induction。

claim: UHAT 对 LTL 呈指数 succinctness gap，同时 LTL→UHAT 仅需 polynomial expansion。
value: exponential lower gap; polynomial reverse expansion
statistical_method: not_applicable；shortest-word witness lower bound + constructive reverse translation。

claim: UHAT 对 finite automata 呈双指数 succinctness gap。
statistical_method: not_applicable；同一 witness family + non-empty automaton shortest-word bound。

claim: UHAT 对 fixed-precision RNN 呈指数 succinctness gap。
statistical_method: not_applicable；Proposition 1 的 RNN→finite automaton bound 与 Theorem 17 合成。

claim: restricted future-leftmost / past-rightmost UHAT non-emptiness 位于 NEXP。
statistical_method: not_applicable；translation lands in NP-complete LTL P/F fragments。

claim: UHAT equivalence 为 EXPSPACE-complete。
comparison: deterministic finite automata equivalence is polynomial-time
statistical_method: not_applicable；reduce emptiness against empty-language UHAT and use LTL equivalence upper bound。
